lyrics:
[Intro: a cappella four-part harmony, no instruments]
Cast iron and a cold one, kids out in the yard

[Verse 1: warm male voice, acoustic guitar]
I've had the kind of money where you don't check the price
Had the kind of trouble where you don't sleep nights
Neither one of them taught me a thing
Like a Saturday with nothing to bring but

[Chorus: full band, fiddle, group singalong]
Cast iron and a cold one, kids out in the yard
Radio on the windowsill, a ballgame from afar
Sun going down like it's got no place to be
A paid-off truck, a porch, and my people around me
It ain't much, and it's all I need

[Verse 2: voice and band, relaxed]
Granddad's skillet, black as a crow
Fed four generations, never touched soap
He'd say, "Rich is a table where nobody's missing"
I didn't get it then. Granddad, I'm listening.

[Chorus: full band, fiddle, group singalong]
Cast iron and a cold one, kids out in the yard
Radio on the windowsill, a ballgame from afar
Sun going down like it's got no place to be
A paid-off truck, a porch, and my people around me
It ain't much, and it's all I need

[Bridge: band drops, fiddle and voice, slower]
Here's to the nurse on the night shift, the lineman in the storm
The teacher buying pencils, keeping thirty kids warm
The ones who keep it running so the rest of us can sit
We'll save you a plate. You've earned it.

[Final Chorus: a cappella first line, then full band]
Cast iron and a cold one, kids out in the yard
Radio on the windowsill, a ballgame from afar
Sun going down like it's got no place to be
A paid-off truck, a porch, and my people around me
It ain't much, and it's all I need

[Outro: fiddle tune, a screen door, children laughing]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 86 BPM, 4/4, G major. An easy back-porch lope; the bridge slows a little and the last chorus picks back up.

VOICE: Male lead, warm, slightly grainy, relaxed. Four voices in tight harmony sing the opening line alone and every chorus. He sings the bridge quietly and seriously.

INSTRUMENTS: Nylon and steel acoustic guitars, fiddle, upright bass, light drums with brushes and a soft backbeat, mandolin, Hammond organ low in the mix. No electric guitar until a short slide part in the last chorus.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, voices alone. 0:10 Verse 1. 0:38 Chorus 1. 1:08 Verse 2. 1:36 Chorus 2. 2:06 Bridge, slower. 2:36 Final chorus, voices alone for one line and then the band. 3:10 Outro, fiddle, door and children, ends 3:28.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Warm, woody and live, like a band on a porch: harmonies wide, fiddle sweet, plenty of air.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The unaccompanied harmony on the title line at 0:00.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original's thanks go to soldiers. This one keeps the gratitude and widens it to the people who keep an ordinary town running, and it is sung by someone who has tried having more.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Looking back, content, thankful, full.
